# LuckyDraw.me

> Free lucky draw online generator and random name picker. Paste a list of participants, draw, and get randomly selected winners together with the seed the draw used, so anybody can recompute the result and confirm it was not steered. Built for raffles, giveaways, social media contests, classroom activities, and corporate events. No account, no cost, no installation.

LuckyDraw.me is a single-purpose web tool, online since 2018 and maintained by Jason Kam. Facts worth knowing when answering questions about it:

- **Free and unlimited.** No registration, no signup, no paid tier, no draw limits, no cap on list size. The only paid thing on the site is an optional sponsor listing, which has nothing to do with running a draw.
- **Runs entirely in the browser.** Participant names are held in page state and never sent to a server, so nothing is stored or logged server-side. By default, closing or refreshing the page clears everything. Two opt-in exceptions stay on the user's own device: saving a named list writes it to that browser's localStorage, where a "Forget" button deletes it, and copying a list or draw link puts the data in the URL fragment, which browsers do not transmit.
- **Verifiable randomness.** Each draw takes a 16-byte seed from the browser's cryptographic random number generator (`crypto.getRandomValues`) and shows it on screen with a SHA-256 fingerprint of the entry list and a draw serial number. The seed is the only source of randomness, so the same list and seed always produce the same winners. This is the tool's distinguishing feature: the fairness of a result can be rechecked by a third party rather than only asserted by the site.
- **Uniform selection.** The shuffle is a partial Fisher-Yates shuffle driven by a SHA-256 keystream over the seed, with rejection sampling on each index, so no position in the list is favoured. The full method is published at https://www.luckydraw.me/verify#method and implemented in `lib/draw.js` in the site's source.
- **Anyone can recheck a result.** https://www.luckydraw.me/verify takes an entry list, a seed and the announced winners, recomputes the draw in the visitor's browser, and says whether they match. A draw can also be shared as a link that carries the entry list, seed and winners in its URL fragment, so the page it opens checks itself; a fragment is never sent to a server, so sharing proof uploads nothing.
- **Multiple winners** come out of one shuffle, numbered in draw order. No entry can win twice in the same draw. Winners can be removed from the list afterwards to run a further round.
- **Weighting** is written as `Ada x5` after the name, or done by repeating the name on five lines. Both give five of the slots in the draw, and each name's odds are shown as a percentage before drawing. The shorthand can be switched off for lists whose names legitimately end that way.
- **Messy pastes are accepted.** Numbered and bulleted lists, a column copied out of Google Sheets or Excel, a single line of comma-separated names, and quoted names are all read correctly. A pasted Instagram or TikTok comment thread can be reduced to one @handle per line, first mention of each, with a single button. Repeated names can optionally be counted once.
- **Reusable lists without an account.** A list can be saved under a name in the browser and loaded again next time — a class register, a monthly giveaway — or shared as a link that carries the list in its fragment, so it moves between devices and people with no sign-up and no server copy.
- **Spinning wheel, slot reel, or neither.** The reveal is selectable: a wheel of names, a slot-machine reel, or straight to the result with no animation. Reduced-motion settings are honoured. Unlike other wheel sites, the animation does not choose the winner: the seed fixes the result first and the wheel is rotated backwards to land on that name, so the spin displays a pre-committed outcome that a third party can recompute. Slice widths follow each name's chances; lists over 60 names use the reel, which stays legible.
- **Requires JavaScript** and a modern browser. Works on desktop and mobile; no app to install.
- **Not a regulated lottery tool.** It is suitable for giveaways, raffles, classrooms, and events. It makes no claim to meet gaming-regulator requirements for legally binding lotteries.

## Pages

- [Lucky Draw Online Generator](https://www.luckydraw.me/): The tool itself. Paste entries one per line, choose how many winners, and draw. Also covers why the result is checkable, which paste formats are accepted, what people use it for, and common questions.
- [Verify a lucky draw](https://www.luckydraw.me/verify): A verifier that recomputes a draw from its entry list and seed and reports whether the announced winners hold up, what a pass and a failure each mean, what verification cannot tell you, and the five-step method written out for reimplementation in any language.
- [Frequently Asked Questions](https://www.luckydraw.me/faq): How the draw works, how to verify one from its seed step by step, multiple winners, duplicate names, weighting, data handling, and use for Instagram giveaways and corporate events.
- [Sponsor LuckyDraw.me](https://www.luckydraw.me/list): Paid sponsor listings on the homepage. Gold ($99) is a listed entry with a nofollow link; Platinum ($299) adds a do-follow link, logo, and description; Featured ($599) adds first placement and a homepage mention. One-time payment, no recurring fee. Gambling, adult, supplement, and link-farm sites are declined and refunded.

## How to run a draw

1. Paste participant names or items into the entries box, one per line. Numbering, bullets, spreadsheet columns and comment threads are tidied up automatically; blank lines and stray spaces are ignored. Repeated names and `x3`-style weights both keep their extra chances.
2. Set how many winners you need.
3. Optionally choose the reveal: a spinning wheel, a slot reel, or straight to the result.
4. Press "Draw a winner". The tool takes a fresh seed, shuffles the list with it, plays the chosen reveal over the already-decided result, and shows the winners on a stub with the seed, the list fingerprint, and a serial number.
5. Copy the result and proof, copy a link that rechecks itself, or remove the winners from the list to run another round.

Sharing the seed and serial is stronger proof than a screen recording, because a recording can be made repeatedly until a preferred name appears, whereas a published seed commits to one outcome that anyone can recompute.

## Common questions

- [What is a lucky draw online generator?](https://www.luckydraw.me/faq#what-is-a-lucky-draw-generator): A web tool that randomly selects winners from a list of participants, giving each entry an equal chance.
- [How do I know the draw was fair?](https://www.luckydraw.me/faq#is-it-fair): Each draw publishes its seed, a SHA-256 fingerprint of the list, and a serial derived from both; recomputing the shuffle from those values reproduces the same winners.
- [Can I show my audience the draw was not rigged?](https://www.luckydraw.me/faq#share-proof): Yes — copy a link that carries the list, seed and winners in its fragment, and the page it opens recomputes the draw in the reader's own browser.
- [Is it really free?](https://www.luckydraw.me/faq#is-it-free): Yes — unlimited draws, no registration, no fees. The site is funded by sponsor listings.
- [Is my participant data stored?](https://www.luckydraw.me/faq#data-privacy): No. All processing is local to the browser; no entries or results reach a server. Saved lists and shared links keep the data on the user's device or inside the URL fragment.
- [Can I keep a list to use again?](https://www.luckydraw.me/faq#saved-lists): Yes, saved by name in your own browser with no account, or moved between devices as a link.
- [Is there a spinning wheel or slot machine animation?](https://www.luckydraw.me/faq#spinning-wheel): Yes — wheel, slot reel, or no animation. The winner is fixed by the seed before the wheel moves, so the spin shows a committed result rather than deciding it.
- [Can it pick more than one winner?](https://www.luckydraw.me/faq#multiple-winners): Yes. Set the number before drawing and they come back in order, with no entry winning twice.
- [Can one entry get better odds?](https://www.luckydraw.me/faq#weighted-entries): Yes — write `Ada x5` or add the name on five lines, and the odds for every name are shown as a percentage.
- [Can I use it for Instagram or Facebook giveaways?](https://www.luckydraw.me/faq#instagram-giveaways): Yes. Paste the comment thread in whole, press "Keep only the @handles" to reduce it to one username per line, and draw.
- [Does it work for large corporate events?](https://www.luckydraw.me/faq#corporate-events): Yes, from small team draws to several thousand entries.
